pr_title: Add some missing NULL pointer return checks
pr_body:
Check the return value after OPENSSL_zalloc() for some EVP types.

We  should also check the return value from OPENSSL_buf2hextr() which may also be NULL.

Fixes #10525.

I agree with @richsalz.

To give credits in a consistent way, I would suggest to use unified tags like `Reported-by:` or `Suggested-by:`, which are used for example in the  [Linux Kernel Sources](https://git.wiki.kernel.org/index.php/CommitMessageConventions).

I did this for example in commit 88d90400c07bd46840b53ecedce370ebe19d9905. 

Your opinion, @openssl/committers?
I think it is a very good practice but it requires a bit more attention that will be missed from time to time.

We have been very sloppy in adding errors to the queue, and we really need to stop that.  This is as good a starting point as any.

issue_context.title: Missing null check after OPENSSL_zalloc
issue_context.body:
Here're places that null pointer check is missing after `OPENSSL_zalloc`. 

1. The pointer `exchange` is used directly in line 23 without being null checked.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/3c957bcd54d097167e53660fa100aa1ba85d63b5/crypto/evp/exchange.c#L21-L23

2. The pointer `signature` is also used directly in line 23. Similar to the first one

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/3c957bcd54d097167e53660fa100aa1ba85d63b5/crypto/evp/pmeth_fn.c#L21-L23

3. In the function `OPENSSL_buf2hexstr`, the result of `OPENSSL_zalloc` is directly returned without null check. The dependents of `OPENSSL_buf2hexstr` are not checking null-pointers too.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/3c957bcd54d097167e53660fa100aa1ba85d63b5/crypto/o_str.c#L242

review_comments: You could cascade this with the lock creation check and have them both set `ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE`

In [line 43/46](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/10526/commits/4c0c53b009d6a3e7a44b43d8238698faf8ad674d#diff-7f75adab80125f8e46d5e500b71fff74R46), you raise an `ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE` when heap allocation fails. Shouldn't this be done consistently for all malloc failures? (several locations)
_Note: if you add new error symbols, take a look at issue #10522 before running `make update`._

The only purpose for the hex value is to distinguish thread IDs in the trace output. So stopping trace output silently is confusing and hard to find. It would be better to send the output anyway, giving a visual indication of the failure:

```C
        BIO_snprintf(buffer, sizeof(buffer), "TRACE[%s]:%s: ",
                     hex != NULL ? hex : "<null ptr?!>", OSSL_trace_get_category_name(category));
```
